requirements.text: A resume trusts every stage that already ran.
Each stage the interrupted run completed counts as done, and its outputs are put back (rehydrated) exactly as they were when the run stopped.
The run picks up at the stage that was interrupted, which runs again from its start.
--from-stage <s> works the same way: every stage before <s> is trusted and rehydrated, and the run starts at <s>.
Amend ADR-006 (resume contract) with the decision above.
Amend ADR-050 §6 to draw the line explicitly between resume (continues the same run, governed by ADR-006) and new-run reuse (earlier run's work, governed by ADR-050 §6).
Rehydration follows the same path the hydrate stage already uses (ADR-050, plugins/tool/hydrate), so "exactly as before" means the same files at the same paths.
A run is interrupted during stage k. Resuming it does not dispatch stages 1…k−1, their outputs are present and byte-identical to what they were at the interruption, and stage k is dispatched. (R1)
Inside a loop (e.g. build → test), a run interrupted mid-round resumes at the interrupted stage of that round. The loop's iteration count and state are restored, not reset. (R2)
--from-stage <s> dispatches <s> first, with every earlier stage's outputs rehydrated. It never emits pipeline.skip_to_stage and then runs an earlier stage. (R3)
--from-stage <s> naming a stage with no prior output to rehydrate refuses with a reason, and does not start. (R4)
Every way to resume (--resume, auto-resume on restart, and zbuild pipeline resume --run-id) finds the interrupted run's state in runs/<run_id>/ and behaves as R1. Each has its own test. (R5)
A run with no prior state behaves exactly as today. (R6)
A new run of the same issue still never skips a stage because of an earlier run's output (ADR-050 §6). (R7)
ADR-006 is in `config/adr-enforcement-baseline.txt`, so the amendment names its enforcing tests inline.
Tests for R1–R5 must use a cycle.
